name: Steppe
notes: Cold, semi-arid temperate grassland of feather grasses, fescues and wormwoods with rare shrubs, treeless except ravines; Eurasian steppe (Ukraine to Mongolia) with Patagonian and Great Basin analogues.

canopy.name: Bristlecone pine
canopy.source: Great Basin high peaks; 5–15 m. Oldest trees on Earth; gnarled, half-dead giants. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

traits.leaf_shape: needles or scale leaves, evergreen (larch deciduous)
traits.trunk: single straight trunk, whorled branches, conical crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.name: Soapweed yucca

repro.note: Yucca moths are the only pollinator (obligate mutualism); if the insect count in the region is zero, seed set is zero and only offsets spread it.

shrub.source: Kew POWO accepted name. Great Plains to the Rockies; rosette form. Traits documented. The cold-hardy plains yucca; trunkless.
